post_text:
Your 99th percentile latency dashboard is lying to you while your database quietly drowns.

Average and percentile metrics hide the catastrophic micro-outages that kill throughput under load.

System health metrics often mask structural decay until a complete cascade occurs. Relying on aggregated dashboards creates a false sense of security.

Average GC pause times look pristine while stop-the-world events target high-throughput threads. Track maximum pause duration and allocation spikes rather than smoothed hourly averages.

This prevents silent queue build-ups.

Low CPU utilization often hides thread pool starvation on critical executor services. When synchronous I/O blocks worker threads, the CPU sits idle while requests time out.

Monitor active thread counts directly.

A high HTTP success rate is meaningless if the failing fraction represents your payment capture endpoint.

Group metrics by business criticality instead of aggregating all API traffic together. This exposes high-value failures.

Stop measuring system averages and start monitoring worst-case execution paths. 🛑
lesson_extracted: Aggregated metrics and averages mask critical, localized system failures under high load.
